sections.h2: What question bank software does here
paras: Question bank software stores every question your institute writes in one organised pool, with the answer, an explanation and tags, so tests can be assembled from it instead of written from scratch each time. In Aura Learn the bank is the source for quizzes, daily practice sets and full mock tests, and all of them are graded from the same answer key.

Faculty add questions one at a time or import them in bulk, tag each by subject, topic and difficulty, and attach the explanation the learner will see in review. When a paper is assembled the platform records which questions were used and where, so the bank shows what has been overexposed and what has never been asked. Analytics on each question show how often learners get it wrong.

sections.h2: Ten thousand questions, spread across documents nobody can search.
sections.lead: Most institutes have written more questions than they will ever need. The problem is finding them, reusing them and knowing which ones actually work.

items.p: Each test is a document, so reusing one good question means finding the paper and copying it out.
Building a topic-wise test means reading through old papers to find questions on that topic.
The answer key exists; the reasoning behind it stays in the faculty member's head.
Nobody knows whether a question is too easy, too hard or simply badly worded.

items.q: Can we import questions we already have?
items.a: Yes. Existing questions can be imported in bulk from a structured file, then tagged by subject, topic and difficulty in the dashboard. Explanations can be imported at the same time or added later by faculty.

items.q: Can one question be used in several tests?
items.a: Yes. That is the point of a bank. A question can be pulled into any quiz, practice set or mock test, and its usage history shows where it has appeared so faculty can avoid overexposing it. See the mock test platform.

After a learner submits, review mode shows each question with the learner's answer, the correct answer and the stored explanation. It is where most of the learning from a test happens, so explanations are worth writing well.

items.q: What analytics come from the bank?
items.a: Per question, how often it is answered wrong. Per batch, topic-wise results. Per learner, the topics they keep missing. Together these show which questions need rewording and which topics need reteaching.

items.q: Does the bank feed the Telegram practice bot?
items.a: Yes. Daily practice sets are drawn from the bank and pushed to learners by the Telegram bot, the same approach used in Elevate Aura's own exam-prep app. See the exam-prep app case study.

items.q: Is the bank separate from the LMS?
items.a: No. It is part of Aura Learn, alongside courses, batches, live classes and fees, so the same bank serves quizzes after lessons and full mock tests. See online quiz platform for the quiz side.
